title: Future Contingents and Relative Truth
version: Published offprint: The Philosophical Quarterly 53(212), July 2003, pp. 321–336; DOI 10.1111/1467-9213.00315; author-hosted 16-page PDF
locator: Selected original clauses and examples: §II printed p.323; §IV pp.326–327; §V pp.328–331, especially Will/Sett clauses p.329 and double-time-reference postsemantics plus sea-battle table p.330–331; selected §VI opening pp.331–332
assumptions: Idealized branching-time model with moments and histories; possible futures through utterance moment; postsemantic evaluation indexed to utterance and assessment contexts. Author explicitly does not presuppose that objective indeterminism is true. Application to a relativistic model is not supplied here.
conclusion: Under the proposed double-time-reference postsemantics, Jake's one sea-battle prediction is neither true nor false when assessed at utterance moment m0, true when assessed from the battle continuation m1, and false when assessed from the no-battle continuation m2. This is assessment-relative utterance truth, distinct from the stable outcome proposition within each complete history.
proof_status: Selected full-text inspection of source clauses and worked example; no formal proof audit, complete paper review, physical reconstruction, or independent semantic implementation.
dependencies: Thomason branching-time supervaluationism and Belnap's double-time references are discussed/cited by MacFarlane; those sources were not audited in this lane.
open_questions: How should the double-context evaluation be adapted to the project's distinct causal-advance and past-agreement relations?
Which assessment-indexed ground signature is appropriate, and can it be motivated without building the truth value into the signature?
What effect should MacFarlane's later published self-assessment of the 2003 argument have on the paired synthesis?
relevance: Primary source for retrospective evaluation of a future-tense utterance; provides exact original clauses and a minimal test case for separating utterance-time truth, later-assessed truth, and fixed-proposition persistence.
limits: Only cited original clauses and example were checked, not every section or the cited literature. This semantic result establishes no temporal ontology, objective passage, physical indeterminism, truthmaker relation, or existence/nonexistence thesis.

title: Papers (John MacFarlane author-maintained publication page)
locator: Entry 30, “Truth in the Garden of Forking Paths,” includes the note that its core ideas come from “Future Contingents and Relative Truth” (2003), whose argument the author now believes inadequate; entry 41 lists the 2003 article. The note is attached to entry 30, not entry 41.
assumptions: Author's retrospective assessment of the 2003 paper's argument; read together with the linked author-hosted garden.pdf preprint for the specific shortcomings stated.
conclusion: The author reports that the 2003 argument was inadequate and that the later paper explains why and gives a more robust argument for the same conclusion. Treat as author self-assessment, not a refutation of the 2003 clauses or result.
proof_status: Publication-page note verified; explanation checked selectively in the linked 2007 preprint, recorded separately as retrospection-macfarlane-garden-2007.
open_questions: The later chapter's full argument and its relation to the 2003 semantics remain outside this bounded audit.
relevance: Correctly locates and scopes the author's self-assessment of the earlier argument.
limits: Short publication-page note; not itself an argument against the 2003 clauses. The explanation was checked only in §1 of the linked preprint.

title: Truth in the Garden of Forking Paths
version: Author-hosted 26-page preprint dated 28 January 2007; later published as a chapter in Max Kölbel and Manuel García-Carpintero (eds.), Relative Truth (Oxford University Press, 2008), pp. 81–102
locator: §1, printed pp. 1–2: author says he aims to correct shortcomings in Future Contingents and Relative Truth (2003), then enumerates three: sentential-operator treatment of temporal modifiers; focus on sentences/utterances rather than propositions and propositional truth, including a supervaluationist response to the retrospective-assessment criticism; and omission of an object-language truth predicate and actuality operator.
assumptions: Branching-time semantic framework; source inspected only for its opening diagnosis and revisions, not its complete theory or proof obligations.
conclusion: The preprint documents MacFarlane's own reasons for calling the 2003 argument inadequate and states that the later work seeks a more robust argument for the same assessment-sensitive conclusion. The self-assessment does not itself refute the earlier clauses or conclusion.
proof_status: Selected full-text inspection of §1 only; no full-paper audit or comparison of all later clauses with the 2003 paper.
dependencies: MacFarlane, “Future Contingents and Relative Truth” (2003), discussed by the author but not re-audited in this source record.
open_questions: How do the later proposition-level and postsemantic clauses resolve the specific retrospective-assessment objection?
Does the later account affect the project's fixed-proposition ground-sufficiency comparison?
relevance: Primary author source specifying the shortcomings behind the author's later assessment of the 2003 argument; corrects the stale locator that attached the website note to the 2003 entry.
limits: Only §1 was checked. No claim that the later chapter refutes or supersedes every 2003 semantic clause; no broad literature survey.
